raw_response:
I farm the way a long-time smallholder around Quzhou would: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to secure grain, make use of my well irrigation, and spread labor across the year. I will still keep a smaller cotton area because I already know how to manage it and it gives me some cash income, but at my age and with part of the family working off-farm, I will not expand cotton too much because it takes more picking and field attention. On the wheat-maize land, I will use better seed, put in enough fertilizer to protect yield, and rely on 2 to 3 irrigations where the crop response is strongest. For wheat, I will push for a stable stand, one good topdressing, and disease control. After wheat harvest, I will put maize straight in quickly so I do not lose summer moisture or growing days. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate when needed through the well, and spray more often than grain crops because insects are usually a bigger problem there. I am not chasing the highest possible input level; I will manage for dependable output, labor I can handle, and lower risk.
